name: RiO-DETRv2
paper_title: RiO-DETRv2: Geometry-Aware Uncertainty Modeling Meets Real-Time Oriented Object Detection Transformer
license_interpretation: Apache-2.0 is a permissive license, so the RiO-DETRv2 code and checkpoints can be used in commercial and closed-source products. Redistributing them means keeping the license text and notices, and the license grants a patent license. About 33 minutes after its initial commit (ab8b22df5d800a927774c8c67e77fd29c0fe6967), upstream changed its LICENSE file to AGPL-3.0; later commits change only the README and LICENSE, not the code. LibreYOLO's port relies on the Apache-2.0 grant of that initial release, uses nothing from later commits, and preserves the Apache-2.0 snapshot at LibreYOLO/RiO-DETRv2 (tag apache-2.0-ab8b22d). The adapted decoder keeps Apache-2.0 with its RT-DETR, D-FINE, DEIM and RT-DETRv4 copyright lines (libreyolo/models/riodetrv2/LICENSE and NOTICE); the HGNetv2 backbone, encoder and decoder blocks reuse LibreYOLO's dfine and rtdetrv2 families, and the wiring around them is LibreYOLO's MIT code. The official checkpoints (Hugging Face RicePasteM/RiO-DETRv2 at revision 5f578f57929aded1962ebf8c5584a4771461124f, tagged apache-2.0) are mirrored as LibreYOLO/LibreRiODETRv2{n,s,m,l,x}-obb (DOTA-v1.0) and -obb-diorr (DIOR-R) with the upstream LICENSE and NOTICE; conversion renames keys and drops a training-only projector, learned tensors are unchanged. The DOTA-v1.0 and DIOR-R training sets carry their own terms.
